facts.label: scripture
facts.quote: The Asuras had three citadels; the lowest was of iron, then there was one of silver, then one of gold. The gods could not conquer them... Rudra let it go; it cleft the Citadels and drove the Asuras away from these worlds.
facts.text: The Taittiriya Samhita of the Krishna Yajurveda contains the earliest textual account of the Asuras constructing three citadels of iron, silver, and gold that Rudra destroyed with a single arrow.

facts.label: scripture
facts.quote: And oh king, as soon as Rudra stood up holding his bow, during that time the three cities united... Shiva destroyed the three flying cities of the asuras with a single arrow.
facts.text: In the Mahabharata's Karna Parva, Shiva as Tripurantaka mounts a cosmic chariot made of the universe and uses a single arrow to destroy the three flying cities of the asura brothers Tarakaksha, Kamalaksha, and Vidyunmali when they align.

facts.label: scripture
facts.quote: The festival is also observed as Tripura Purnima Snan. The main rituals performed by devotees consist of kartik snan and deepdan.
facts.text: The Skanda Purana associates the full moon of Kartik with the celebration of Tripuri Purnima and prescribes the ritual bath and lighting of lamps along the riverfront.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: The ancient site of Tripuri is situated nearly 2 km south west from Tewar village. During 2020-21 ASI conducted excavation of Tewar at two locations, TWR 1 and TWR 2.
facts.text: Archaeological excavations at the ancient site of Tewar confirmed that it corresponds to Tripuri, an ancient city settlement dating back to the late Chalcolithic and early historic periods.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: 'Tirpuri', the Prakrit form of the name, can be found on copper coins dated to the 2nd century BCE or earlier.
facts.source_name: Archaeological Survey of India / Sagar University
facts.text: Excavations at Tripuri recovered copper coins bearing the city name in ancient Brahmi and Prakrit script dating to the second century BCE.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: Most of the ghats were rebuilt after 1700 AD, when the city was part of the Maratha Empire. The patrons of current ghats are Marathas, Shindes, Holkars, Bhonsles, and Peshwes.
facts.source_name: Archaeological Survey of India / UNESCO Tentative List
facts.text: Architectural and archaeological surveys record that the masonry stone steps across the eighty-four river ghats of Varanasi were primarily constructed and paved between the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries CE under Maratha patronage.

facts.label: legend
facts.quote: Mythologically, the gods are believed to descend to Earth to bathe in the Ganges on this day. The festival is also observed as Tripura Purnima Snan.
facts.text: According to local oral belief in Varanasi, thirty-three crore deities descend to earth on Kartik Purnima to bathe in the Ganga and celebrate Shiva's victory over the demon Tripurasura.

facts.label: disputed
facts.quote: The tradition of lighting the lamps on the Dev Deepawali festival day was first started at the Dashashwamedh Ghat by Pandit Kishori Raman Dubey (Babu Maharaj) in 1991.
facts.text: While popular belief views the synchronized riverfront lighting across all ghats as an ancient multi-millennial ritual, local records document that the modern collective festival of Dev Deepawali was initiated in 1985 at Panchganga Ghat and expanded in 1991 at Dashashwamedh Ghat.

facts.label: disputed
facts.quote: The alignment of the three moving cities once in a millennium has been interpreted either as an astronomical planetary conjunction, an allegory for cosmic dissolution, or a purely symbolic metaphysical narrative.
facts.text: Scholars disagree on whether the myth of three moving cities aligning in the sky reflects an ancient astronomical observation of a planetary conjunction or meteor impact, or serves strictly as an allegorical Vedic ritual construct.

facts.label: scripture
facts.quote: Akashdeep is offered with the intention of pleasing Lord Vishnu and for the welfare of ancestors during the holy month of Kartik.
facts.text: The traditional practice of hoisting Akashdeep lamps inside wicker baskets atop tall bamboo poles throughout the month of Kartik is documented in the Skanda Purana as an ancestral offering predating the modern mass Dev Deepawali spectacle.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: ASI is carrying out excavation at archaeological site of Tewar... The architectural findings mainly consist of a brick wall and sandstone columns which are yet to be exposed fully as the project is ongoing.
facts.source_name: Archaeological Survey of India Lok Sabha Starred Question 197
facts.text: Excavations conducted by the Archaeological Survey of India at Tewar in 2021 revealed sandstone columns, brick walls, and early historic artifacts demonstrating long-term systematic urban occupation.

intro.prompt: 16:9 landscape, 1920x1080, about 8 seconds, photorealistic and cinematic, bright vivid colour. Setting: night aerial view of the Varanasi ghats on the Ganga blazing with endless rows of oil lamps, thin smoke and mist, crowded wooden boats, temple spires lit gold, the lower fifth calm dark river water reflecting the lamps. The background is real and in motion behind him (as fits the place: waves, mist, leaves, flags, lamps flickering, people walking, traffic, light shifting); never a still, flat or heavily blurred backdrop. If the scene shows the past, it is ancient India: Indian people in dhotis, sarees and angavastram, warriors with bows, spears and bronze or leather armour, carved stone pillars, oil lamps; never European knights, plate armour, castles or anything medieval European. Framing: medium shot from the waist up, his whole head and both shoulders inside the frame with clear space above his hair and on both sides, and he stays framed like this to the end; do not crop the top of his head. Lighting: warm key light on the face, a soft rim light on the hair, matched to the scene; flattering, no harsh shadows, no dull or flat grey look. SG [locked] standing relaxed and upright, shoulders open, wearing an olive green kurta. Speaks from the first frame, mouth matched to the words, steady eye contact with the lens. Face and delivery: a confident, charismatic documentary presenter. Calm, natural face with a pleasant, warm smile, relaxed eyebrows, eyes soft and focused on the viewer. On "ya sirf 1985 se" the eyes narrow a little with intrigue and the head tilts slightly, as if sharing a secret. On "Ruko, asli khel abhi baaki hai!" a warm, confident smile and one small nod. Natural blinking, subtle head movement. No exaggerated expressions: no wide eyes, no raised eyebrows, no open-mouth surprise, no big grin, no frown; never sad, gloomy, worried or tired. Voice: warm, clear, measured, with quiet intensity; a short pause before "ya sirf 1985 se". Hands: one slow, small gesture toward the scene behind him on the first line, then hands rest; no fast or large arm movements. Camera: eye level, a very slight slow push-in, slight handheld feel. Empty hands, no prop. @SGMythWorld watermark in the top right corner, white, bold, 80% opacity. No captions, no subtitles, no other on-screen text. No hologram, no floating screen, no graph, no chart, no laptop, tablet, monitor, TV or glowing blue panel anywhere in the frame. Export at 1920x1080.
